subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec treat PowerShell `$...` expansion syntax as a supported command-fidelity case that enters explicit one-shot approval, or should inline `$...` PowerShell remain unsupported/documented with script-file guidance?
rationale: Current source rejects the syntax and the viable repair changes exec approval semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent command-fidelity and approval-boundary contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the explicit-approval fix
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 or a similar patch, but require real Windows/Gateway proof before landing.

options.title: Document script-file workaround
options.body: Decide that inline PowerShell `$...` syntax is unsupported and update exec docs/tool guidance instead of changing approval behavior.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Keep this issue open only for a maintainer-supplied or reporter-supplied Windows transcript before selecting runtime or docs work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the explicit-approval fix
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 or a similar patch, but require real Windows/Gateway proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is centered on the Windows shell analysis and exec approval planner that jesse-merhi introduced in c9707ab635b9.
